status: retrospective development experiment; no public model change
question: Does already observed upstream rain improve the frozen hydrometric model before reservoir discharge or river stage responds?
inputs: Use exact-hour level/flow dataset and audited regional rain windows. A rain feature at origin t ends at t-1h; never use future observed rain. Require at least 50% regional coverage for every 3, 6, 12 and 24h window in all five regions. Missing rain excludes a row from both paired arms, never becomes zero.
pairedArms: Keep the public model's selected hydrometric feature family and per-horizon ridge alpha. Refit the hydrometric arm and a second arm with 20 extra observed rain features on exactly the same rows. No model or alpha selection from validation or test in this experiment.
splits: Training targets before 2025-10-01 00:00 BRT; validation origins after 33h embargo with targets before 2026-07-01 00:00 BRT. Refit on training plus validation, then evaluate test origins after 33h embargo with targets before 2026-09-21 00:00 BRT. The previously inspected September flood is a separate stress set.
rainFeatures: For each of Baixo Antas, Carreiro, Prata-Turvo, Alto Antas and Tainhas: area weighted observed rain in 3, 6, 12 and 24h, divided by 100mm. All windows end one hour before origin.
assessment: Report paired MAE and fraction within 0.50m for each 1-6h horizon, high water >=7m, rapid rise >=1m relative to origin, and rain strata >=20, >=50, >=100mm regional 6h maximum. Report a quiet-hydrometry plus rain stratum and false alarms. Do not claim independent generalization, calibrated flood risk or operational availability from retrospective data.
